questions.q: How did Comstock turn her introversion into an advantage at GE?
a: She listened and observed instead of forcing her way in
She avoided meetings and worked alone on projects
She hired allies to speak for her in discussions
She challenged the men directly in every meeting
questions.why: Lesson 1 says she used her ability to listen and observe, engaging with ideas rather than taking exclusion personally.

questions.q: What did Comstock do after the September 11 attacks?
a: She ran a full-page ad of the Statue of Liberty rolling up her sleeves
She cancelled all company advertising for the year
She moved GE's offices out of New York City
She launched a campaign asking employees to donate
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes the ad as the message of hope people needed, and many hung it on their walls.

questions.q: Why did Comstock push the Statue of Liberty ad despite resistance?
a: She believed the workforce needed a message of hope
She wanted to advertise a new GE product line
She was following orders from the CEO
She hoped it would boost the company's stock price
questions.why: Lesson 2 says she saw that employees were deeply shaken and an uplifting message was vital.

questions.q: What does Comstock say every uncertainty contains?
a: An opportunity that a good story can help you seize
A warning that the company should cut costs
A reason to wait until conditions improve
A test of whether your strategy is sound
questions.why: Lesson 3 says every uncertainty has opportunity baked into it, and the right story unlocks it.

questions.q: How did Comstock help GE employees after the financial crisis?
a: She told a story about where the company was headed
She promised that no one would lose their job
She offered everyone a bonus to raise morale
She brought in consultants to redesign strategy
questions.why: Lesson 3 says a powerful story of the struggle and its future got people moving again.
